R1.description: The unattended prune selects only archives of class finished, older than unattended.ttl_days (strictly), whose review folder is already absent, never an id under an interrupted removal, at most prune_max_per_run, oldest first, from a fresh complete report; an archive whose folder still exists is never selected (the wedge hazard)

R2.description: Dry-run equivalence: the engine's prune dry run for exactly the planned set must list exactly that set before any --apply; any difference stops the run; the apply is one id per call with --ttl-days passed explicitly

R3.description: Every safeguard of the unattended run stays: preflight, authority, policy re-read before every engine call (also unattended.prune), audit-first, the first failure stops the run, one audit line per prune action and refusal (step prune), a prune failure leaves the earlier steps done and reported

R4.description: retention-cleanup --unattended runs the prune phase after a cleanup phase that did not stop when unattended.prune is true; --json gains the prune section with schema_version unchanged; exit codes keep their meaning

R5.description: status, doctor, the adopt preview, the cleanup preview and docs/retention.md say that prune is run unattended with its exact limits, that deleting an archive cannot be undone and where the archive store lives; docs/exit-codes.md is updated; ROADMAP row 52 is added and marked Done; tests and goldens cover every refusal and stop with failure-only mutations
